items.text: – You did the best thing, Nini-jan. They say newborns need a lot of sleep. Ten hours a day.
items.q: Nini, the children's pet name for Maman, means newborn. Does the teasing land?

items.text: – Yeah, right.
items.q: Asked if he was calling, Farid means of course I was. Is that clear?

items.text: – Oh-ho. Hamid Cat, until yesterday you said "ass." Now you've gone all civilized and say "donkey"?
items.q: Taghi mocks Hamid for swapping a rude word for a polite one. Does it land?

items.text: In a way, you could say they conquered the university. Karroubi is love, honestly and truly.
items.q: Farid is excited. Does 'Karroubi is love' sound like natural student slang?

items.text: – Is Arasteh a trimmed-down Araasteh?
items.q: The family dropped one a from Araasteh (Persian: neat). Is the joke clear?

items.text: I press the elevator button. The elevator door opens. That day, Niloofar had come up the stairs. I go toward the stairwell. The voices of a boy and a girl drift out of the elevator. They call me sick.
items.q: The riders mock him for calling the elevator, then walking off. Does 'sick' land?

items.text: – And with that dickish way you talk, your name should've been Alain Dickon. Don't flatter yourself. I don't mean Alain Delon, with the way you scrunch up your nose ...
items.q: Hooman's insult puns on the actor Alain Delon. Does 'Alain Dickon' land?

items.text: – In my opinion, life is like a thousand-toman banknote: whichever side you look at, it smells of lentil rice.
items.q: Meysam ends a deep debate about life with a silly quip. Does the joke land?

items.text: After that, like a screw with stripped threads, that image was no longer bound to the darkness behind the closed door of our house.
items.q: The memory came loose from that one place. Is the screw image clear?

items.text: – It's marmal stone. Marmal means really expensive.
items.q: A boy mispronounces marble and thinks the word means expensive. Is that clear?

items.text: – Yeah, I've heard a few things about this localization business.
items.q: This means the regional quota for university places. Is 'localization' clear here?

items.text: He can't help it. That's just his factory setting. Always so elegant and formal, shitting right at the historic turning point.
items.q: Hooman mocks Amir for messing up at a key moment. Does this read naturally?

items.text: – Last night I could hear you ruminating. Too bad my Baba was asleep, otherwise I'd have gotten up and pulled every single sweet out of your throat.
items.q: Eskandar teases Hooman for chewing sweets at night like a cow. Does 'ruminating' land?

items.text: – But he fucked it up. Eagle Eye says peer-to-peer; Taverny says Eldie-to-Eldie.
items.q: Amir (Taverny, Eldie) misheard peer as pir, Persian for elder. Does the joke land?

items.text: – Kids, we've been watching a movie at our relatives' house.
items.q: A schoolboy addresses his friends. Does 'Kids' sound natural from him?

items.text: They saw the red and all their body hair fell right out, objectively.
items.q: This means they got a sudden fright. Is the meaning clear?

items.text: With that toy car he pulled along behind him, he would surely fall from Negar's eyes.
items.q: This means Taghi would lose Negar's respect. Is the meaning clear?

items.text: That Dr. Shafiʿi Kadkani had taken my poem and said he'd read it later? Just a harvest-time promise?
items.q: A harvest-time promise means an empty, put-off promise. Is the meaning clear?

items.text: It makes you shit-dizzy. The more you think about it, the more shit-dizzy you get.
items.q: A student's crude made-up word for baffling. Does 'shit-dizzy' work as slang?

items.text: They dumped earth over her with a buldozel. Earth and lime.
items.q: Maman mispronounces bulldozer on purpose. Is that clear?
